text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 7142 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- The Hungarian government in an official statement expressed its concern over the tense situation in Serbia regarding the manipulation of local election results. @
- Former finance minister Lajos Bokros spoke out on the controversy surrounding the privatisation of Budapest Bank, adding that the debate is politically motivated.
- The Socialists have set a deadline of March 31 for reaching cross-party consensus on a new constitution.
- Minister of Culture Balint Magyar announced that the administration plans to make the Internet available in high schools by the end of 1997-1998. (Sat.) @

- The Budapest Court has set the date of the first trial in the Tocsik affair for January 22. Nepszabadsag reports today that Tocsik has withdrawn those parts of her confession which affect the Socialist Party and Free Democrat treasurers.
- The president of the Democratic Forum addressed an opposition rally in Belgrade Saturday.
- Exports are expected to grow by at least 6 percent but not more than 8-9 percent this year.
- The consumer price of pharmaceuticals will go up by an average of 12 percent from Wednesday. @
- An unidentified person tossed a Molotov cocktail into a pub in Budapest on Saturday causing damage but no injuries.
- A Molotov cocktail burnt down an all-night videotheque in Budapest Friday night.
MAGYAR HIRLAP
- Interior Ministry and the Ministry of Agriculture have reached an agreement in principle on dividing the tasks of the Compensation Office ahead of its planned winding-up.
- Negotiations have started between the State Privatisation and Holding Co. and the Belgian company Tractebel regarding the January energy price hikes. @
- The Ministry of Industry and the Hungarian Enterprise Development Fund along with several banks will start a programme to develop the automotive and electronic support industries in Hungary.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Consumer prices rose 0.9 percent in December, bringing year-on-year inflation to 19.8 percent.
- Net average wages totalled HUF 31,040 in January - November, 19.5 percent more than the same period of the previous year, the Central Statistics Office reports. @
- Companies are expected to spend more on advertisements this year than in either of the last two years, said Peter Nagy, chief secretary at the Hungarian Advertising Association.
- As of January, companies investing into the infrastructure in some of Hungary's "special zones" may receive a 6 percent tax allowance.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. is expected to invite bids for the closed privatisation of Takarekbank Rt. by January 20. @
- The Board of Directors of the national telecoms company Matav decided Thursday that Merrill Lynch will manage the introduction of its shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
NEPSZABADSAG
- The London office of the Nomura investment bank admitted to having misjudged the performance of the Budapest Stock Exchange last year in its latest report.
- The Rome daily La Repubblica has reported that the German government continues to pay pensions to 1,337 Hungarian SS volunteers who were wounded during World War II.
-- Budapest newsroom (361) 327 4040
